# KOYASH Product Roadmap

Project: **KOYASH**  
Team: **Sunwise (#12)**

This roadmap describes the planned MVP evolution for the course project. It is intentionally incremental: each MVP version should produce a coherent user-facing slice and be validated with the customer before the next iteration.

## MVP v1 — Sprint 1

**Sprint Goal:** Deliver the first working slice where a user can understand KOYASH, complete a branded questionnaire, send answers to the backend, and see an explainable skincare routine generated by rule-based logic.

| Story | Description |
|---|---|
| US-01 | Landing page explains trust, independence, and warm CTA |
| US-02 | Step-by-step questionnaire: age, skin type, concerns, exclusions, budget |
| US-03 | Budget selection by controlled segments |
| US-04 | Allergens and unwanted ingredients as hard constraints |
| US-05 | Rule-based recommendations from product database |
| US-06 | Personal cosmetic bag shown as a routine |
| US-07 | Explanation for each recommended product |
| US-14 | Why-we-ask explanation on every questionnaire step |
| US-15 | Explanation-first product cards and readable routine |

Total estimate: **44 Story Points**.

### Sprint 1 Customer Review Focus

Sprint 1 is validated through a customer review with Diana. The review focuses on:

- whether the MVP v1 user flow is understandable;
- whether the questionnaire and recommendation logic match customer expectations;
- whether the design direction, palette, gradient, and light background should be continued;
- which visual corrections should be made before release;
- which backlog items should be considered for Sprint 2.

## MVP v2 — Sprint 2

Scope to be confirmed with the customer after Sprint 1 Review.

Candidates from backlog:

| Story | Description |
|---|---|
| US-08 | Open product and consultation links |
| US-09 | Give feedback when a product does not fit |
| US-10 | View previous recommendations |

Expected Sprint 2 refinement topics:

- improve product data field coverage;
- refine product feedback flow;
- decide whether recommendation history requires identity/session storage;
- continue visual polish based on customer-approved direction.

## MVP v3 — Sprint 3

To be defined after Sprint Review with the customer and after Sprint 2 refinement.

Possible future directions:

- better product dataset coverage;
- improved recommendation scoring;
- more complete routine structure;
- deeper feedback analytics;
- optional dashboard after MVP validation.

## Excluded

| Story | Reason |
|---|---|
| US-12 | Excluded — privacy, accuracy, medical, and technical risks |
| US-11 | Removed from backlog |
| US-13 | Removed after customer clarification |

## Assignment 4 / Sprint 2 roadmap update

### Current increment: MVP v1 final

MVP v1 focuses on:

- landing page and visual direction;
- guided skincare questionnaire;
- cosmetic bag / recommendation result;
- product reasoning;
- product feedback action;
- customer-reviewed design direction;
- quality requirements and quality requirement tests;
- automated checks and CI evidence;
- deployment/access documentation.

### Customer feedback follow-ups

Based on the customer review / facilitated UAT walkthrough, the following improvements are tracked as follow-up work:

- improve logo visibility and placement;
- strengthen the main headline visual hierarchy;
- adjust landing page spacing and composition;
- revise visual assets that do not match the desired tone;
- restructure landing information blocks;
- continue palette and typography exploration;
- improve filtering and personalization.

### MVP v2 candidates

The following items are candidates for MVP v2:

- deeper recommendation filtering;
- stronger product dataset and rule mapping;
- fuller frontend/backend integration;
- browser-based end-to-end tests;
- improved deployment automation;
- repeated customer validation with direct customer interaction through deployed link.

### Release direction

The Assignment 4 release is published as `v0.2.0`. It represents a quality-controlled MVP v1 increment with documentation, validation evidence, tests, CI checks, and deployment/access information.

## Assignment 5 / Sprint 3 roadmap update

### Current increment: MVP v2

MVP v2 turns the MVP v1 prototype into a working, integrated product:

- frontend connected to the backend API (questionnaire, recommendations, auth);
- real personalized recommendations with prices and explanations;
- product feedback → replacement suggestion flow;
- previous recommendations / account history;
- containerized deployment on the university VM (single-port nginx + reverse-proxy);
- architecture documentation (static/dynamic/deployment views) and ADRs;
- development-process documentation and updated quality/UAT artifacts.

### Customer feedback follow-ups (deferred to next sprint)

Detailed visual feedback from the MVP v1 review is grouped into one design-overhaul
backlog item (#50) so it can be applied consistently, aligned with the designer's
mockups:

- bolder typography (Montserrat bold);
- smaller, more square elements; consistent margins;
- remove dashed line; lighten main blocks; adjust logo placement;
- center step icons with equal spacing;
- rename budget labels (Бюджетный / Средний сегмент / Люкс);
- trim confusing questionnaire questions;
- limit custom input length (~100 chars);
- product image sourcing/scaling strategy.

### Next increment: MVP v3

- design overhaul aligned with the designer's mockups;
- deeper recommendation filtering and scoring;
- questionnaire content cleanup;
- LLM-assisted explanations after MVP validation.

### Release direction

The Assignment 5 release is published as `v0.3.0`. It represents the integrated,
deployed MVP v2 increment with architecture documentation, ADRs, development-process
documentation, updated tests, UAT evidence, and deployment/access information.
## Assignment 6 / Sprint 4 (Week 6) roadmap update

### Current increment: MVP v3 trial (v0.4.0)

Week 6 delivers an integrated trial toward the final MVP v3:

- working backend across the end-to-end flow (questionnaire → profile → history);
- current frontend wired to the live API for the customer trial;
- customer trial + UAT + Sprint Review conducted with the customer, Diana;
- design approved (with minor edits) as the final MVP v3 direction;
- full documentation set, CI running the full backend test suite, and the v0.4.0 trial release.

### Customer feedback follow-ups (Week 7 / Sprint 5)

From the Week 6 review, tracked as issues:

- #61 validate and fix budget filtering (per-product) — customer validates on 3–5 samples;
- #62 fix replacement category matching (a cleansing gel must not replace a cream);
- #50 apply the approved design 1:1 and add explicit morning/evening labeling;
- #63 LLM prompt update and joint evaluation with the customer;
- #64 repository and secrets handover after the defense.

### Next increment: MVP v3 final (Week 7)

- validated filtering and corrected replacement logic;
- approved design applied 1:1;
- LLM prompt evaluation with the customer;
- public MVP v3 demo and final release;
- repository and secrets handover.

### Release direction

The Week 6 trial is published as `v0.4.0` (trial increment). The final MVP v3 is planned
as `v0.5.0` in Week 7.

## Assignment 6 / Sprint 5 (Week 7) roadmap update

### Current increment: MVP v3 final (v1.0.1)

Week 7 delivers the final MVP v3:

- redesigned, more functional frontend shipped as the final direction (#50);
- product catalog and favorites removed as out of concept (#65);
- detected skin type shown on the questionnaire result (#66);
- guest cosmetic bag preserved by signing in (#67);
- validated per-product budget filtering (#61);
- corrected in-category product replacement with the correct number of alternatives (#62);
- finalized LLM explanation prompt, disabled by default (#63);
- customer transition completed, `v1.0.0` release followed by the audited `v1.0.1`
  patch, public demo evidence, and Demo Day preparation.

### Customer transition

- Handover level: `Ready for independent use` (university VM deployment).
- Customer confirmation status: `Accepted with follow-up items`.
- Post-defense follow-up: repository and secrets handover (#64). The customer-authored
  prompt and filtration-sample contract are integrated in the final deployed build.

### Release direction

The final MVP v3 is published as `v1.0.1` (Semantic Versioning) on the protected default
branch, mapped to the Sprint 5 milestone. It is the final course state: the roadmap does
not invent a speculative post-course version. The only remaining transition action is
the agreed secure repository and secrets transfer after the defense (#64).
